## Historical audit: H0027

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_formal_04/codex_formal_04_B_r4/infer_logs/anko-default-function-arguments/turn_1/trajs.json`. Event references below are to its `main_agent` events; offsets are character ranges in the supplied observations.

| Area | Evidence and assessment |
|---|---|
| Goal | The task name and reproduction suggest a goal of supporting default function arguments. The original task instructions and intended semantics are not visible, so that goal is inferred rather than a complete specification. |
| Autonomous exploration | The student inspected the grammar, generated parser, AST, function binding and argument-count checks (events 3–4, chars [0,11910); 7–10, chars [0,35814) and [0,18762)). Further inspection covered AST traversal and scanner positions (events 13–18). One `rg` pattern produced an error, but the enclosing command continued (event 14, chars [0,7614)). |
| Actual changes | The student created branch `default-arguments` from `master` (events 5–6, chars [0,796) and [0,3002)); a later status showed the branch without listed file changes (event 16, chars [0,9956)). A temporary reproduction file was created and removed (event 11, chars [0,798)). The student reported no implementation or commit (event 19, chars [0,971)). |
| Validation and outcome | Running `func f(a = 2) { return a }; println(f())` produced `Execute error: syntax error`, exit status 4 (events 11–12, chars [0,798) and [0,430)). The supplied inventory reports a zero-byte patch, **0/2 fail-to-pass and 119/119 pass-to-pass**, formally not solved. These are reported evaluation results, not evidence of a working implementation. The run ended normally; this is an empty-patch outcome, not a demonstrated failure of a submitted algorithm. |
| Teacher input | The inventory lists available shared hints and an actual-system-prompt path, but their contents are not supplied here. No delivered teacher text appears in the visible events; receipt and adoption therefore cannot be established from availability. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, a minimal reproduction can establish the starting failure while repository exploration identifies relevant layers without establishing a fix. Task-specific evidence shows identifier-only function parameter grammar and fixed-arity checks; the student attributed non-completion to uncertainty about safely changing checked-in generated parser tables (events 10 and 19). Whether regeneration or another approach would have solved the task remains untested. The exact requested default-evaluation semantics and the contents of any captured system prompt remain unknown.
